verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. I rendered spec_p829.png at 300 dpi and read it against page-829.md line by line. Printed page 799 (PDF page 829) contains exactly: the running head 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', '15.3.1 Format arguments to international date and time functions', '15.3.1.1 General', its paragraph, NOTE 1, the 'A single format describes...' paragraph, NOTE 2, NOTE 3, the 'COBOL supports six date formats...' paragraph, '15.3.1.2 Calendar date formats' + 2 paragraphs, '15.3.1.3 Permissible values for data associated with calendar date formats' + 3 paragraphs, '15.3.1.4 Ordinal date formats' + 1 paragraph, and the footer. Every one of those headings and paragraphs is present in page-829.md with identical numbering and identical title text. Zero words are missing, altered, reordered, or added. The kind 'missing-heading' is factually wrong for this page. (2) THE CLAIM MISQUOTES THE PDF ON THE PAGE UNDER TEST. It asserts the PDF page 829 reads '15.3 Arguments ... 15.3.1 ...'. It does not. '15.3 Arguments' is not on this page at all: the rendered page begins with 15.3.1 as its first line of body text. In the markdown, `### 15.3 Arguments` at line 33366 sits under ` ## Page 826`, three pages earlier. A page-829 finding cannot be grounded in a heading that appears on page 826. (3) THE ASSERTED 'CONVENTION' DOES NOT EXIST — the depth is non-semantic transcription formatting, document-wide. Counting the whole transcription: X.Y.Z-numbered headings are emitted 276x as `##`, 508x as `###`, 17x as `####`; X.Y-numbered headings are emitted 162x as `##` and 26x as `###`. Within clause 15 itself, 97 of the 100 `15.x` headings are `##` and only three (15.1, 15.2, 15.3) are `###` — so `## 15.3.1` is one of hundreds of instances of the majority pattern, and the outlier is `### 15.3` on page 826. The claim's own cited exemplars are self-contradictory: it offers `### 15.5.1 General` as the convention while `## 15.4.1 Numeric and integer functions`, `## 15.3.2 Time formats`, `## 15.3.3 Common time formats` and `## 15.5.3 Standard date form` are all level 2. Decisively, the page-boundary markers themselves are `## Page 829`, i.e. level 2, the same depth as `## 15.3.1` — the `#` count in this transcription carries no hierarchy semantics anywhere, so no local defect exists to fix on page 829. (4) NO MEANING CHANGES, AND THE HIERARCHY IS NOT LOST. The section numbers are literal text in every heading ('15.3.1.1'), and each heading is preceded by a correct hierarchical anchor (``, ``, ``). Any TOC or section tree is built from those numeric labels/anchors, which are exact and complete; the '#' count is decoration. Nothing normative — no syntax, no general rule, no permissible-value range — differs between the PDF page and the markdown. This is a cosmetic markdown-depth artifact of the whole transcription, misfiled as a page-829 content discrepancy and mis-typed as 'missing-heading'. If the owner ever wants uniform heading depth, that is a single global normalization pass over ~800 headings, not a per-page spec-reconciliation ledger entry.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. Page 829 (printed 799) transcribes verbatim and completely: 15.3.1, 15.3.1.1 + NOTE 1-3, 15.3.1.2, 15.3.1.3, 15.3.1.4 with all body paragraphs intact. No heading is missing. The cited '15.3 Arguments' is on page 826, not 829. The reported level inversion is a document-wide, non-semantic markdown '#'-depth artifact (X.Y.Z headings: 276 '##' / 508 '###' / 17 '####'; page markers themselves are '## Page NNN'), and within clause 15 the '##' form used here is the majority (97 of 100), so page 829 is not even the outlier. Section hierarchy is fully recoverable from the literal section numbers and the correct '<a id="section-15-3-1">' anchors.
